messages:
maria: heads up — noticed a steady increase in tiny-pod pending counts across two racks in us-west2 after yesterday's DR drain. small pods (0.25/0.5 GPU) are getting shelfed, fragmentation up ~18% vs baseline.

maria: dashboard -> https://redwood.internal/gpu/frag?range=6h (filter: us-west2-rack-3,rack-4)

devin: which scheduler version? any recent weight rollouts?

sasha: metrics: pending_small_pods=137, avg_wait=4.2m, gpu_util_gap per-rack ~0.65, orphaned_slots=24.

kai: looks like the drain left lots of 1-slot freebies on different nodes — scheduler prefers AZ spreading so tiny pods get scattered instead of coalesced.

jon: we tried a compacting weight bump last quarter and saw tail-latency blips on bigger training jobs. can we canary it to a single rack?

maria: yes — propose a 2-hour canary on us-west2-rack-3: enable soft-coalesce with scoreBoost=0.6 limited to label "coalesce-canary=west3-1". fallback policy immediate.

devin: sounds good. cost note: current wasted GPU-hours estimated ~40 GPU-hrs/day (~$2.8k/week on spot pricing) if fragmentation stays.

kai: config patch I suggest:

```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.redwood/v1
kind: SchedulerPolicy
metadata:
  name: coalesce-canary-west3
spec:
  nodeSelector: { "rack": "us-west2-rack-3" }
  coalesce:
    enabled: true
    scoreBoost: 0.6
    maxBundleSlot: 2
```

maria: can someone run the canary and watch preemptions? also we should temporarily increase warm-pool size on that rack by +4 to absorb bursty tiny pods.

devin: I'll open the rollout. steps: 1) apply policy 2) scale warmpool 3) enable monitor alert for small-pod preempt > 5/min 4) rollback after 2h or on error.

devin: kubectl patch command I'll run:

```bash
kubectl apply -f coalesce-canary-west3.yaml --context=us-west2 && 
kubectl -n infra scale deploy/warmpool-usw2-rack3 --replicas=6
```

jon: add a short-lived trace in the runtime to collect KV cache hit/miss for coalesced tiny pods — helps us measure perf impact.

sasha: hooking up the evals dashboard — will track pending count, pod start latency, preemptions, and affected customer routes. link will be in the rollout thread.

ops-bot: alert: gpu_pool_us-west2 pending_small_pods threshold breached (137) — created incident INC-2026-198.

maria: assigning owners: devin (rollout), kai (scheduler tweak), sasha (metrics/evals), jon (runtime trace). target start in 20m.

devin: starting canary now. will post status every 5m.

deploy-bot: canary deployment coalesce-canary-west3 started by devin at 1719804680 — step 1/3 applied.

maria: if we see >10 preempts in 10m or rps drop for customer-chat, abort.

devin: 5m update: pending_small_pods down to 82, avg_start_latency improved to 1.8m, preempts=0. rolling on.

jon: trace shows tiny-pod KV hit rate unchanged, no tail spikes so far.

sasha: cost projection if sustained fragmentation fix -> save ~28 GPU-hrs/day.

devin: 2h summary: pending_small_pods stabilized ~35, orphaned_slots reduced to 6. no customer impact observed. rolling policy to rack-4 as a cautious next step.

maria: follow-ups: (1) prod-runbook note about canary flags, (2) consider permanent scheduler policy with dynamic warm-pool auto-scale, (3) postmortem if we re-enable spread bias.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-198 resolved by policy canary and warmpool scaling.

maria: thanks everyone — great quick coordination. :tada:
